items.title: Australian-first mass police AI pilot sparks concern
items.description: More than 130,000 faces have already been scanned under WA Police's landmark facial recognition trial. The privacy watchdog, experts and Aboriginal advocates are raising concerns about who could be caught in its net.

items.title: Live: Government target vulnerable species for bird flu vaccines
items.description: Agriculture Minister Julie Collins has announced the federal government will be moving to vaccinate birds in captivity over the coming days and weeks against the H5 strain of bird flu. Follow live.

items.title: This international student helped Bondi attack victims. It could cost him
items.description: Abdullah Ashraf, a law student from Pakistan, had his student visa lapse while on compassionate leave from his studies in the aftermath of the Bondi Beach terror attack.

items.title: Live: Search continues for survivors after 111 die in Colombia earthquake
items.description: The government has declared a national emergency following the tremor, which struck at 7:34am local time (10:34pm AEST). Follow live.

items.title: The RBA's big challenge: How to navigate a real estate downturn
items.description: Deflating a property bubble takes some skill, something that has escaped almost every government or central bank that has ever attempted it.

items.title: Live: ASX opens higher as no changes expected to interest rates
items.description: The Aussie share market opens higher as the Reserve Bank is expected to keep the cash rate steady at 4.35 per cent in August. The central bank will also release its updated economic forecasts, including the inflation, growth and unemployment outlooks. Follow live.

items.title: 'They will be taken over': Warning for Philippines as dispute with China erupts
items.description: Foreign Correspondent journeys to one of the world's most contested islands where China's shadowy 'maritime militia' lurks just off the coast.

items.title: 'Ah, sorry guys': Pilot's reaction after Antarctic mishap damages plane
items.description: An accident that damaged an Australian-contracted aircraft in Antarctica has triggered new safety protocols on the icy continent, internal government documents show.

items.title: What happens if you do not complete your census form?
items.description: Census 2026 is here. This is the lowdown on how it works and whether there is a fine for not completing the form.

items.title: Why Trump selling early access to his posts is causing controversy
items.description: For up to $US100,000 per month, subscribers can receive the US president's Truth Social posts milliseconds before everyone else. But experts say the bigger question is whether some traders are already getting information much earlier.

items.title: Federal police urged to investigate 'concerning' subsea cable fault
items.description: Two subsea cables off the coast of Perth, vital for international communications, suffered a fault over the weekend, and the company that owns them urgently wants to know what happened.

items.title: Super experts explain ways to get your affairs in order
items.description: Millions of Australians could have no say in who inherits their superannuation. Here's how to check if you're one of them, and how to make sure your wishes are followed.

items.title: 'Loyalty doesn't pay': Car insurers asked to explain soaring premiums
items.description: The corporate regulator ASIC has taken aim at major car insurers, finding the companies are not explaining why customers' premiums are rising faster than inflation.

items.title: First look at designs for new Town Hall Square 'in the heart' of Sydney
items.description: The new public square will be opposite Town Hall in the heart of Sydney's CBD, promising "the grandeur of a European square".

items.title: The absurdity of Aussie rules football inspires new comedy video game
items.description: Mixing 1990s-era gameplay aesthetics with silly power-ups, Pro Jank Footy has fun with a national obsession.

items.title: Debut memoir reveals what it's really like to be a woman in her 30s today
items.description: Sheree Joseph always wanted to write the Great Australian Novel. Instead, her first book is a memoir about what happens when life doesn't live up to expectations.

items.title: Quiz: Does Australia have more baristas or personal trainers?
items.description: Today's More or Less quiz challenges you to rank different occupations by how many people do them.

items.title: Limp Bizkit return to headline loud and proud Aussie festival
items.description: Good Things has rallied another big selection of metal, punk, emo and more for the east coast this December.

items.title: Calvary considers new Launceston hospital at aged care site
items.description: A private hospital operator has confirmed it is considering a new hospital in Tasmania's north, two years after it cancelled plans for a $130 million development.

items.title: Mehreen Faruqi says her Australianness feels 'conditional'
items.description: Ask Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi what she was like as a child and you'll catch a revealing glimpse of her as an adult.

items.title: Big Tex leaves big impact on and off the field
items.description: Taylor Walker arrived at the Adelaide Football Club as a 75-kilogram prospect who had only ever wanted to be a footballer. More than 300 AFL games and 700 goals later, he will retire as a club great.

items.title: 'Evidence is clear': Players association says brutal schedule behind injuries
items.description: As the Canadian Open gets underway with several big names sidelined, it is evidence that the current tennis schedule is unsustainable, according to the PTPA.

items.title: Why did Israel reject Donald Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza?
items.description: Israel's rejection of Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan is not a surprise. Here's why and how politics plays into it ahead of an Israeli election.

items.title: Why SA is holding a royal commission into AI
items.description: South Australia pioneered the global push to restrict children's access to social media. Could the state's royal commission into AI also lead to national policy?

items.title: Potholes force cars off Calder Freeway as Victorian road anger rises
items.description: Maintenance crews are patching up potholes on the Calder Freeway between Gisborne and Sunbury after at least seven cars were damaged this morning.
